## Active

### D-053 — Kopi generates its own screenshots instead of a demo realm

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The screenshot demo first created a throwaway `dev/testrealm` (a rush.json entry plus lockfile
changes), which contradicted the directive not to create new realms. The realm was reverted and
`core/blong-kopi` itself became a runnable realm that generates its own screenshots.

### D-054 — A seed whose method has no handler needs a real handler

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The kopi seed crashed because of a stale handler, not because of `$`:
`meta/dbTest/$subject$ObjectMerge.yaml` and `$subjectAuthorizationMerge.yaml` dispatched methods
with no handler, since the master-detail refactor had deleted the custom Add handler.
`$subject$ObjectMerge` resolves through the generic `exec` fallback (like blong-marine's
`marineCoralMerge`), but `$subjectAuthorizationMerge` needed a real handler, so
`adapter/db/$subjectAuthorizationMerge.ts` was added as a simplified `accessAuthorizationMerge`.

### D-055 — The scaffold template reuses the shared RBAC merge handler

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The kopi template's `adapter/db/$subjectAuthorizationMerge.ts` was not needed: blong-access's
`accessAuthorizationMerge` handler is fully generic — it processes any
`user`/`role`/`capability`/`policy` names and has no access-specific logic — and it is attached to
the `db` adapter in every suite (access is a child realm, and `srv.db` imports `/.db$/`). The
duplicate existed only because the seed was named `$subjectAuthorizationMerge.yaml`, so its derived
method `$subject.authorization.merge` had no handler; renaming the seed to
`meta/dbTest/accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml` makes the fixed file name derive
`access.authorization.merge` and dispatch to the SHARED handler. Only the seed CONTENT carries
`$subject` placeholders (substituted per realm at scaffold time), so scaffolded realms always reuse
the framework handler and the template stays minimal. Verified: kopi tap 6/6 (RBAC 401/403/200 plus
the permissions assertion) and Playwright 4/4.

### D-303 — The realm template ships a Storybook whose story kind renders model pages

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · active_

blong-kopi had no Storybook, so no scaffolded realm had one. The story the storybook descriptor
generates is the model page story (page of subject object browse, open, new and report), not a
component story: a realm React page is produced by the model system, while a component primitive
emits a server-side handler that no story can import, so a generic component story cannot be
generated. main and preview come from the shared blong-browser factories, and preview composes
index.browser.ts rather than browser.ts because a model page needs the portal port that only the
composed entry carries.

### D-304 — The template globs meta fixture, unlike the marine realm

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · active_

blong-marine globs only meta/model and its orchestrator, so its meta/fixture handler is never loaded
by the browser platform and its stories read an empty data set. The template does the opposite:
browser.ts globs meta/fixture as well, and kopi ships a fixture whose rows mirror the seed yaml, so
a scaffolded realm stories have data out of the box. meta/type and meta/db stay out of the glob
because they are server-side and would not bundle. The marine realm should be aligned with this,
which is recorded as a todo.

### D-308 — A scaffolded realm gets the template tree, not its bookkeeping

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The template package is also a real package, so it carries things that belong to it rather than to a
realm scaffolded from it: its own manifest fields, its `.github/memory` entries, and its generated
report folders. Both scaffolders now rewrite the manifest through the shared `scaffoldManifest`
(name `@feasibleone/blong-<realm>`, version 0.1.0, a description of the realm) instead of copying it
— the package name is what a suite imports and what the dev database name is derived from, so the
bare folder name it used to keep gave a new realm a database name unlike every other package. The
memory folder is excluded rather than scaffolded empty, because `blong-dev memory add` creates the
file with that realm's header the first time it runs there; a copy could only ever be another
package's notes. `.ci-report` and `coverage` moved into the same shared ignore list, where until now
they existed only in kukum's own skip set and so still reached `blong realm`.

### D-311 — The generated marker covers .tsx, so a scaffolded story is stamped

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The marker decides ownership of a generated file, and the merge engine treats .ts and .tsx as the
sources that carry it. Both scaffolders stamped only .ts, so every .tsx the template ships — the
Storybook preview and the two stories — arrived without a marker and was refused as hand-written the
first time the same kind was re-added: a story could be generated into a realm and then never
refreshed, with only a warning to say why. Stamping moved behind one shared predicate in
blong-lib/template, which createRealm, kukum template planning and the merge engine now all read, so
the three cannot disagree about which files a scaffolder owns again.

### D-312 — The realm name is the folder without its blong- prefix

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · active_

A realm folder is named `blong-<realm>` in this monorepo, but the template substitutes the bare
name: it becomes the subject namespace (marine.entry.add), identifiers inside the generated handlers
(async function marineFixture), unquoted object keys, file names and the method names derived from
the seed files. createRealm used to take the folder basename verbatim, so blong realm blong-marine
scaffolded a realm whose story, fixture and model handler did not parse, and it failed as late as
Vite could get to the file, long after the scaffold reported success. Both scaffolders now render
through one shared helper, scaffoldSubject, which drops a leading blong- and refuses a name it could
not substitute before anything is written, so the auto-trigger fails with the reason instead of
writing a broken realm. The prefix is added back where the template needs the package or app name
(blong-$subject, import('@feasibleone/blong-$subject/browser.ts')), which is why the manifest still
names the package @feasibleone/blong-marine. kukum's realm check stays stricter: it validates the
name a caller passes rather than a folder it derives from.

### D-331 — The template fixture mirrors the seed ids so a story loads in both backend modes

> _2026-09-30 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The fixture carried ids 1 and 2 while meta/dbTest seeded 101 and 102, and the Open story opened
record 1, so mock mode worked while live mode opened an empty form. The fixture and the Open story
moved to 101 rather than the seed moving to 1: the seed is what a browse screenshot baselines, and
changing it would have rewritten the committed Playwright baselines. Names keep the seed wording
plus a (fixture) marker, which is what makes the Backend item visibly do something.
